Struct ContractSelfUtility

pub struct ContractSelfUtility<Storage, CallSelf> {
    pub address: AztecAddress,
    pub storage: Storage,
    pub context: UtilityContext,
    pub call_self: CallSelf,
}

Core interface for interacting with aztec-nr contract features in utility execution contexts.

This struct is automatically injected into every external contract function marked with "utility" by the Aztec macro system and is accessible through the self variable.

Type Parameters

  • Storage: The contract's storage struct (defined with storage, or () if the contract has no storage
  • CallSelf: Macro-generated type for calling the contract's own utility functions (same type as CallSelf in [PrivateUtilityCalls])

Fields

address: AztecAddress

The address of this contract

storage: Storage

The contract's storage instance, representing the struct to which the storage macro was applied in your contract. If the contract has no storage, the type of this will be ().

This storage instance is specialized for the current execution context (utility) and provides access to the contract's state variables.

Developer Note

If you've arrived here while trying to access your contract's storage while the Storage generic type is set to unit type (), it means you haven't yet defined a Storage struct using the storage macro in your contract. For guidance on setting this up, please refer to our docs: https://docs.aztec.network/developers/docs/guides/smart_contracts/storage

context: UtilityContext

The utility execution context.

call_self: CallSelf

Provides type-safe methods for calling this contract's own utility functions.

Example API:

self.call_self.some_utility_function(args)

Implementations

impl<Storage, CallSelf> ContractSelfUtility<Storage, CallSelf>

pub fn new(context: UtilityContext, storage: Storage, call_self: CallSelf) -> Self

Creates a new ContractSelfUtility instance for a utility function.

This constructor is called automatically by the macro system and should not be called directly.

pub unconstrained fn msg_sender(self) -> AztecAddress

The address of the contract that made this function call.

This is similar to Solidity's msg.sender value.

Direct Invocation

A utility function invoked directly (e.g. by a wallet or dApp) rather than from another contract has no caller, and this function panics. Only a nested (cross-contract) utility call has a msg_sender.

If you need to handle the no-caller case, use UtilityContext::maybe_msg_sender.

Note that utility functions are simulated client-side and never proven, so this value is unconstrained: see UtilityContext::maybe_msg_sender for why it must not be relied on as a security guarantee.

pub unconstrained fn call<let M: u32, let N: u32, T>( _self: Self, call: UtilityCall<M, N, T>, ) -> T
where T: Deserialize

Makes a utility contract call from another utility function.

The call runs entirely offchain in PXE and is never proven, so no guarantees are made on the correctness of its result.

The callee observes this contract's address as its msg_sender: see ContractSelfUtility::msg_sender.

To call one of this contract's own utility functions, prefer the type-safe self.call_self stubs.

Authorization

A call to this contract itself always succeeds. A call to a different contract can expose that contract's private state to the caller, so it requires explicit authorization. A call that is not authorized fails.

Example

self.call(Token::at(address).get_balance_of(owner));
